candidates.rule: Hand-written lists inside `.github/` that mirror repository state (the provider inventory in issue templates, locale/namespace inventories in agent SKILL.md files) must be generated or validated by a prek/pre-commit hook rather than maintained by hand
candidates.trigger: A PR adds a manually enumerated list of providers, locales, or i18n namespaces to `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*.yml` or `.github/skills/**/SKILL.md` without a corresponding hook entry in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`

candidates.rule: A new pre-commit hook's `files:` pattern must be narrowed to exactly the distributions and subpackages the rule applies to; never a bare `\.py$` or a whole-distribution glob
candidates.trigger: A new `- id:` block in `.pre-commit-config.yaml` uses `files: \.py$` or a broad `^providers/<dist>/(src|tests)/.*\.py$` for a check that only holds in part of that tree

candidates.rule: Any query whose rows are dereferenced through an ORM relationship inside the scheduler loop must eagerly load that relationship (e.g. `joinedload(DatasetEvent.dataset)`); default lazy loading is not acceptable there
candidates.trigger: Scheduler-loop code builds a set or log line by accessing `event.dataset.uri`, `record.dag.<attr>` or similar on rows from a query carrying no `joinedload`/`selectinload` option

candidates.rule: In GitHub Actions steps do not `source .venv/bin/activate` after `uv venv`; uv commands pick up the project virtualenv on their own
candidates.trigger: A workflow `run:` block contains `uv venv` followed by `source .venv/bin/activate` before `uv pip install`

candidates.rule: When dropping a `needs:` gate to parallelise a release workflow, split the publish/sync steps into a job that still `needs:` the gating job instead of discarding the ordering guarantee outright
candidates.trigger: A job in a release workflow has its `needs:` replaced (e.g. `needs: [publish-docs-to-s3, build-info]` becomes `needs: [build-info, build-ci-image]`) while it still contains sync or publish steps that must not land before the gating job

candidates.rule: The version dropdown in `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/1-airflow_bug_report.yml` must list only currently released, non-yanked versions; a yanked release is rolled back until `main` is bumped to its replacement
candidates.trigger: A PR adds or leaves a version string in the bug report template's `options:` list for a release that has been yanked or not yet cut

candidates.rule: Adding a new UI locale - a `locales/<code>/` line in `.github/CODEOWNERS` plus its translation files - requires reaching out on the dev@airflow.apache.org mailing list to establish and confirm that locale's owners
candidates.trigger: A PR adds a new `airflow-core/src/airflow/ui/public/i18n/locales/<code>/` entry to `.github/CODEOWNERS`, or a new locale directory, with no reference to a dev-list thread

candidates.rule: Do not add hand-written documentation pages that enumerate REST API endpoints or their schemas; the auto-generated `stable-rest-api-ref` page already publishes them
candidates.trigger: A new `.rst` file under `airflow-core/docs/` documents an API surface (endpoints, request/response shapes) that is already generated from the OpenAPI spec

candidates.rule: A new provider-governance policy section in `PROVIDERS.rst` must state its applicability to already-existing providers - either that it applies only to providers created after the governing AIP's approval date, or how existing providers are transitioned
candidates.trigger: A PR adds a governance section (stewardship, lifecycle, ownership requirements) to `PROVIDERS.rst` stating requirements without scoping them to new versus existing providers

candidates.rule: Documentation of provider attic status must spell out the CI and maintenance consequences: not actively tested in `main`, dependencies not checked for conflicts with other providers, common refactorings not applied, and significant effort required to restore the provider
candidates.trigger: A PR describes provider lifecycle or attic status listing only that modules stay readable and unmaintained, without the CI, dependency-conflict and refactoring consequences

candidates.rule: Treat `providers/edge3/.../worker_api/` and `.../plugins/` as the server side and `.../cli/` as the client side: server-only imports such as FastAPI, and checks that assume server context, must not reach the `cli` subtree
candidates.trigger: A path-scoped check, import rule, or FastAPI/server-side import applies to all of `providers/edge3/` rather than excluding `providers/edge3/src/airflow/providers/edge3/cli/`

candidates.rule: Classify a change to the serialized structure of triggerer context data as a breaking provider change, alongside behaviour changes in `execute()`/`poke()`/`get_conn()` and xcom/connection/asset schema changes
candidates.trigger: A provider PR alters the fields or shape of data a Trigger serializes into triggerer context, and the changelog or documentation classifies it as a feature or bugfix rather than breaking

candidates.rule: Locale guideline files under `.github/skills/airflow-translations/locales/` must use the same heading format as the existing ones - the language name plus the locale code only, e.g. `# Thai (th)`
candidates.trigger: A new `locales/<code>.md` file opens with a descriptive heading such as `# Thai (th) Translation Guidelines for Apache Airflow` instead of `# Thai (th)`

candidates.rule: A locale guideline file adapted from another locale's document must carry over every glossary term from the source, including deliberately untranslated ones such as `Dag ID`
candidates.trigger: A new or updated `locales/<code>.md` glossary omits terms that the locale document it was derived from lists

candidates.rule: In translation guidelines, the keep-in-English term list applies only to CamelCase code/class identifiers quoted verbatim as code (`TaskInstance`, `DagRun`, `Triggerer`); when the same concepts appear as UI labels they must follow the wording already in that locale's `i18n/locales/<code>/*.json`
candidates.trigger: A locale guideline file lists `TaskInstance`, `DagRun` or similar CamelCase identifiers under a blanket keep-in-English rule without distinguishing code identifiers from UI labels

candidates.rule: Write the term as `Dag`/`Dags` in user-facing prose - release notes, changelog entries and UI strings - never `DAG`/`DAGs`; the casing is treated as case-sensitive
candidates.trigger: A new bullet in `RELEASE_NOTES.rst`, a changelog entry, or a translated UI string spells the term `DAG` or `DAGs`

candidates.rule: Every provider extra added to the root `pyproject.toml` must pin a minimum provider version (`apache-airflow-providers-<name>>=X.Y.Z`), matching the surrounding extras
candidates.trigger: A new entry is added to the extras tables in `pyproject.toml` as a bare `"apache-airflow-providers-foo"` with no version specifier while neighbouring extras carry `>=` bounds

candidates.rule: `uv.lock` changes in a PR must match that PR's code diff; regenerate the lockfile against fresh `main` to strip rebase artefacts such as unrelated extras or dependency removals
candidates.trigger: A PR's `uv.lock` diff adds or removes dependencies (e.g. dropping `langchain-openai` from an extra) that nothing in the PR's source changes touches

candidates.rule: Docs and newsfragment prose must use the Airflow 3 spellings of core nouns: `Dag`, `Dag run`, `Dag files`, `Dag bundles`, `Dag Processor`, `API Server` (never `DAG`, `webserver`, or `DAG processor`), while generic concept words stay lowercase (`email notifier`, not `email Notifier`) unless they name an actual class
candidates.trigger: A `.rst` docs page or newsfragment adds prose containing `DAG`, `DAG run`, `DAG files`, `webserver`, `DAG processor`, or capitalises a generic concept noun that is not a class name

candidates.rule: When docs enumerate a feature's parameters, each bullet must name the exact keyword argument in double backticks (``reference``, ``interval``, ``callback``) and the stated mandatory/optional counts must match the real signature
candidates.trigger: A docs page lists parameters as capitalised prose words (`Reference:`, `Interval:`, `Callback Kwargs:`) or claims a number of mandatory parameters that disagrees with the constructor signature

candidates.rule: Security-model guidance that narrows credential distribution must keep connection credentials available to the Dag processor and triggerer; only the JWT signing key is withheld from components that neither generate nor validate tokens (workers)
candidates.trigger: `security_model.rst` or deployment guidance adds advice that connection credentials should be available only to the API server, without carving out the Dag processor and triggerer

candidates.rule: A `.feature.rst` newsfragment must state what the new API does for users, not the internal defect it fixes: "check whether a user is authorized to approve a HITL task", not "to fix ApprovalOperator authorization"
candidates.trigger: A newsfragment sentence is phrased as "... to fix <internal component/behaviour>" instead of describing the capability the change adds

candidates.rule: A `.significant.rst` newsfragment that ticks the Behaviour-change or Code-interface-change checkbox must spell out the delta in prose: "Previously it worked as X, now it works as Y" / "Previously the interface was X, now it is Y"
candidates.trigger: A `.significant.rst` file marks `[x] Behaviour changes` or `[x] Code interface changes` but contains no before/after explanation of what changed

candidates.rule: A significant newsfragment describing an observability or process-management change must add the operator-visible impact and migration step (dashboards built on the old Gauge must move to Histogram aggregations; how to roll-restart the api-server on Kubernetes)
candidates.trigger: A `.significant.rst` describes an internal representation or process change (metric instrument type, uvicorn worker/restart model) without saying what existing deployments must do about it

candidates.rule: Do not add a newsfragment for a documentation-only change; a `.doc.rst` fragment for a pure docs update is overkill
candidates.trigger: A PR whose diff touches only files under `docs/` also adds a file under `airflow-core/newsfragments/`

candidates.rule: Partition mapper classes must be named `To<Granularity>Mapper` (`ToHourlyMapper`, `ToDailyMapper`, `ToWeeklyMapper`, `ToMonthlyMapper`, `ToQuarterlyMapper`), not the bare granularity name
candidates.trigger: A new partition mapper class, or documentation of one, uses a bare granularity name such as `HourlyMapper` or `DailyMapper`

candidates.rule: Profiling and other developer-only libraries (e.g. `memray`) must be declared as an optional extra in `airflow-core/pyproject.toml`, never appended to the mandatory `dependencies` list
candidates.trigger: A diff adds an entry to the top-level `dependencies = [...]` array in `airflow-core/pyproject.toml` for a tool that only some users need

candidates.rule: Cross-team asset-event triggering must ship with the most restrictive default (a teamless API user may trigger only teamless consumers) and the restriction must be documented with the reasoning behind it
candidates.trigger: Multi-team documentation or code defines which producers may trigger which consumers across team boundaries, and either proposes a permissive default or states a rule with no explanation

candidates.rule: In `multi-team.rst`, feature-specific sections belong above the concluding multi-team architecture diagram, which is meant to end the page
candidates.trigger: A new section is appended after the `multi_team_arch_diagram.png` image block in `airflow-core/docs/core-concepts/multi-team.rst`

candidates.rule: Architecture docs must say the scheduler reads serialized Dags from the metadata database and needs no direct Dag bundle access, and must not assert that another component (e.g. the triggerer) accesses bundles directly without verifying it
candidates.trigger: A docs diff enumerates which Airflow components require access to Dag bundles or Dag files

candidates.rule: `curl` examples in the docs must percent-encode reserved characters in the query string (`%7C` for `|`, `%5E` for `^`) or use `curl --data-urlencode`, so the example runs when copied verbatim
candidates.trigger: A `.. code-block:: bash` block adds a curl invocation whose URL query string contains a raw `|`, `^`, or other RFC 3986 reserved character

candidates.rule: A language-SDK docs page that documents log forwarding must also document the configuration the SDK already reads for it — for the Java SDK, `AIRFLOW__LOGGING__LOGGING_LEVEL` and `AIRFLOW__LOGGING__NAMESPACE_LEVELS`
candidates.trigger: A new Logging section under `airflow-core/docs/authoring-and-scheduling/language-sdks/` lists the integration artifacts but has no subsection on setting log levels

candidates.rule: A new row in `extra-packages-ref.rst` must describe exactly the component types the provider ships (hooks, triggers, queue providers, operators); do not write "hooks and operators" for a provider that defines no operators
candidates.trigger: A diff adds a row to the extras table in `airflow-core/docs/extra-packages-ref.rst` whose description does not match the components actually defined in the corresponding provider package

candidates.rule: A PR's title and description must describe the scope actually present in the diff; a documentation/CI/repo-metadata-only change must not be titled as a CLI or behaviour fix
candidates.trigger: PR title or description claims a code/CLI behaviour change (e.g. "map_index bounds validation") but the diff touches only docs, CI configuration, or repo metadata

candidates.rule: `AsyncCallback` must wrap something that is actually awaitable; synchronous notifiers such as `SlackWebhookNotifier` expose no awaitables and must not appear inside `AsyncCallback` in deadline-alert examples or Dag code
candidates.trigger: `AsyncCallback(` is constructed with a notifier or callable that defines no async interface, in docs examples or in deadline configuration

candidates.rule: Do not describe the Execution API as an "internal" API; describe it as an API for use by Airflow itself rather than third-party callers, because it is deliberately reachable from outside the deployment
candidates.trigger: Security or API documentation introduces the Execution API with the word "internal", or implies it is not exposed outside the deployment boundary

candidates.rule: The UI authentication JWT must be stored in a secure, HTTP-only `_token` cookie with `SameSite=Lax`, never in browser local storage or local settings
candidates.trigger: Auth-manager or UI code, or documentation of it, stores or describes storing the `access_token` anywhere other than the secure HTTP-only cookie

candidates.rule: Execution API JWTs are minted by the scheduler via the executor's `jwt_generator` property while the workload is built; `executor.queue_workload()` must not generate tokens, it forwards whatever workload it is given
candidates.trigger: An executor implementation creates or refreshes a task JWT inside `queue_workload()` (or elsewhere in the executor) instead of consuming the token already present on the workload

candidates.rule: Connection-listing methods in auth managers must account for all connection sources (env vars, secrets backends, etc.), not only the database; a DB-only query must be documented as returning a partial list
candidates.trigger: New method on BaseAuthManager queries Connection table without considering non-DB connection sources

candidates.rule: Any new public method added to BaseAuthManager that introduces user-facing behaviour must be accompanied by a newsfragment and a defined default behaviour for auth managers that do not override it
candidates.trigger: New method added to BaseAuthManager (or subclass) without a newsfragment file and without a documented/implemented default fallback

candidates.rule: Do not shorten ILIKE performance-warning descriptions in filter_param_factory docstrings; the explicit version ('ILIKE \'%term%\' prevents B-tree indexes, prefer prefix_pattern') is required to guide operators on large tables
candidates.trigger: Performance note in filter_param_factory description shortened or replaced with an abbreviated form that omits the ILIKE expansion and index guidance

candidates.rule: The API representation of infinite pool slots must use -1, not None; JSON cannot represent float('inf') and None conflicts with the existing API spec for open slots
candidates.trigger: Serialiser or Pydantic validator converts float('inf') pool slots to None before returning an API response

candidates.rule: List routes in the FastAPI core API must use the paginated_select convention for all DB-backed collections; omitting pagination on a collection endpoint is not acceptable
candidates.trigger: New GET list route in api_fastapi/core_api/routes/public/ returns all rows via session.scalars(select(...)).all() without calling paginated_select

candidates.rule: All exception types that a service function can raise must be caught at the route level; when a dry-run variant catches an exception (e.g. DagRunTypeNotAllowed) the non-dry-run counterpart must catch it too
candidates.trigger: except tuple in a route handler is missing an exception type that the called service function is documented to raise, while a sibling route (e.g. dry-run) already handles it

candidates.rule: Do not duplicate a DB lookup at the route level when the same lookup already occurs inside the service function; raise a domain exception from the service and catch-and-convert it at the route level instead
candidates.trigger: Route handler calls session.scalar/session.get for a model that the downstream service function already queries for the same purpose

candidates.rule: Broad AirflowException catches at route boundaries must not forward arbitrary internal error messages as 4xx detail strings; narrow the catch to user-facing exceptions or validate the message before re-raising
candidates.trigger: except AirflowException as e: raise HTTPException(4xx, str(e)) without narrowing the caught exception type or filtering the message

candidates.rule: Authorization checks must short-circuit the query path entirely; do not pass an empty list to XComModel.get_many (or equivalent) as a proxy for 'no results' when the user is unauthorized
candidates.trigger: result_task_ids = [] or equivalent empty-collection sentinel used to suppress results after a failed authorization check, instead of returning early before the query

candidates.rule: Aggregate statistics over DagRun history (durations, averages) must not be computed by fetching unbounded result sets; pre-compute them incrementally or use windowed queries, and confirm migration safety before adding new computed columns
candidates.trigger: select() over DagRun with no row limit used to compute aggregate statistics (avg duration, p90, etc.) in a route handler

candidates.rule: Bulk DAG updates must use a single subquery-based UPDATE (DagModel.dag_id.in_(subquery)) rather than paginated SELECT loops that issue one DB query per page
candidates.trigger: paginated_select or offset/limit loop used to fetch DAG IDs before issuing individual UPDATE statements in a bulk-patch route

candidates.rule: Response models must not include fields already available through a separately fetched resource on the same page; check existing endpoint payloads before adding redundant fields to a datamodel
candidates.trigger: Field added to a Grid/collection response datamodel (e.g. GridRunsResponse) that duplicates data already returned by a companion detail endpoint called by the same UI view

candidates.rule: Do not use runtime inspect() introspection to detect whether a provider-supplied auth-manager override accepts a parameter; perform the parameter-presence check on the caller side and pass the argument conditionally
candidates.trigger: inspect.signature() or inspect.Parameter used inside BaseAuthManager to detect whether a subclass method accepts a specific keyword argument

candidates.rule: Config values read inside hot paths (called once per task during scheduling) must be cached at construction time, not re-read on every call
candidates.trigger: conf.get* called inside a method that is invoked per-task or per-DAG-run in the scheduler loop rather than once at object construction

candidates.rule: Database error handlers in the FastAPI exception layer must follow the existing per-dialect pattern; do not add new string-sniffing markers for individual error sub-types without matching the established dialect-aware structure
candidates.trigger: New tuple of string markers (e.g. _TOO_LARGE_MARKERS) added to an exception handler in api_fastapi/common/exceptions.py without dialect-specific branching

candidates.rule: DataError exception messages surfaced to API clients must be generic enough to cover all possible DataError sub-cases, not worded as if only one specific cause (e.g. text-size overflow) can trigger them
candidates.trigger: HTTPException detail string inside a DataError handler mentions a specific column type (MEDIUMTEXT, LONGTEXT) or a single error cause

candidates.rule: When exposing SQL statement details via conf expose_stacktrace, retrieve sensitive fields (statement, orig) only after the guard check, not before; default them to None rather than a placeholder string
candidates.trigger: getattr(exc, 'statement', ...) or getattr(exc, 'orig', ...) assigned before the expose_stacktrace config check inside an exception handler

candidates.rule: SQLAlchemy JSON column type checks must use isinstance(col.type, JSON) for cross-dialect compatibility; do not add a string-comparison fallback (str(col.type).upper() in ('JSON','JSONB')) unless you can confirm isinstance fails for a specific dialect
candidates.trigger: str(self.attribute.type).upper() in ('JSON', 'JSONB') used alongside isinstance(self.attribute.type, JSON) in a filter parameter

candidates.rule: Task-group filters on list endpoints must use exact group-id matching, not pattern/prefix matching, to avoid returning TaskInstances from unrelated groups
candidates.trigger: TaskInstance list filter applies pattern matching (LIKE / regex) against task_group display_name or group_id

candidates.rule: Single-value filter parameters on list endpoints should accept multiple values (list[str] with FilterOptionEnum.ANY_EQUAL) so callers can request several items in one request instead of needing a dedicated GET /{id} endpoint
candidates.trigger: filter_param_factory used with a scalar type (str | None) for a unique-key field (e.g. uri, conn_id) on a list endpoint that could naturally accept multiple values

candidates.rule: DagModel subqueries that filter by file location must also include bundle_name to correctly scope results across bundles
candidates.trigger: select(DagModel.relative_fileloc).distinct().subquery() without bundle_name column

candidates.rule: Every HTTP status code a FastAPI route can actually raise must be declared in the route decorator's responses dict so the OpenAPI spec and generated clients include it
candidates.trigger: raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_4xx_...) inside a route whose @router decorator lacks that status code in responses={}

candidates.rule: Execution-API JWT data models should expose only the scope field needed at the application layer; JWT validation fields (exp, aud, iss, nbf, iat) belong in the upstream JWTValidator, not in the application-level token model
candidates.trigger: Pydantic model for an execution-API token including JWT standard claims (exp, aud, iss, nbf, iat) alongside application-level fields like scope

candidates.rule: Regex-based query parameters in the execution API must use a _pattern suffix to match the public REST API naming convention
candidates.trigger: Annotated[str | None, Query(description='... pattern ...')] parameter whose name does not end in _pattern

candidates.rule: AssetEvent.extra filtering in execution-API routes must use _parse_extra_params() and JsonContains() rather than ad-hoc string splitting on '='
candidates.trigger: for item in extra: if '=' in item: k, v = item.split('=', 1) pattern applied to AssetEvent.extra

candidates.rule: Execution-API asset resolvers must filter by AssetModel.active.has() when resolving an asset by name, to prevent workers from reading or writing state against removed assets
candidates.trigger: select(AssetModel.id).where(AssetModel.name == name) inside an execution-API route without .where(AssetModel.active.has())

candidates.rule: JWT generation for the execution token must occur inside the same try/except block that commits the TaskInstance state transition, so a token-generation failure does not leave a TI committed as running without a token
candidates.trigger: execution_token = generator.generate(...) or response.headers['X-Execution-Token'] = ... placed after the try/except that commits TI state

candidates.rule: OpenAPI HTTP exception description strings within the same route file must consistently either all end with a period or none do
candidates.trigger: create_openapi_http_exception_doc([...]) call where some description strings end with '.' and others do not within the same file

candidates.rule: Do not use hasattr(state, 'value') guards on Airflow state enum types; all TerminalTIState, TerminalStateNonSuccess, and TaskInstanceState values always have .value
candidates.trigger: hasattr(some_state, 'value') pattern used with a variable typed as TerminalTIState, TerminalStateNonSuccess, or TaskInstanceState

candidates.rule: Remove TODO comments that document conclusions of already-completed investigations; if the conclusion is 'no easy way to achieve this', delete the comment rather than leaving it in code
candidates.trigger: # TODO: comment in execution_api routes where the investigation has already concluded it is infeasible

candidates.rule: Multi-team validation error messages shared across connections, pools, and variables routes must be extracted into a single shared constant to avoid drift
candidates.trigger: identical multi_team error message string literal duplicated across two or more of connections.py / pools.py / variables.py

candidates.rule: Error messages that cite 'manually triggered' as the reason logical_date is None must also cover asset-triggered DAG runs, which equally have logical_date=None
candidates.trigger: error message string containing 'manually triggered' adjacent to a logical_date is None check on a DagRun

candidates.rule: Task-group pattern resolution logic invoked from a public API endpoint must reside inside the corresponding QueryTI filter class's to_orm method, not be inlined in the route handler
candidates.trigger: resolve_task_group_pattern_to_task_ids or equivalent task-group expansion code placed directly in a route function rather than in a QueryTI* subclass

candidates.rule: Do not use inspect to probe clear_task_instances function signatures at runtime; fix tests to pass expected arguments directly
candidates.trigger: inspect.signature or 'params' in params pattern used to conditionally pass arguments to clear_task_instances

candidates.rule: Removing an existing public REST API query parameter is a breaking change; keep the old parameter and add the new one alongside it
candidates.trigger: diff removing a Query parameter (e.g. xcom_key) from a public route that previously exposed it

candidates.rule: Logic used exclusively by a public API endpoint must not be placed under the ui/ service layer; move it to a common or public service module
candidates.trigger: service function inside api_fastapi/.../services/ui/ being imported or called from a public/ route

candidates.rule: Dashboard DAG state counts (active, failed, running, queued) must use a consistent semantic baseline—either all based on latest run or all based on any run—so counts cannot exceed the total number of DAGs
candidates.trigger: dashboard query mixing latest-run state with any-run state counts in the same response (e.g. failed uses latest_state while running/queued use any DagRun in that state)

candidates.rule: Skip calling _serialize_xcoms() entirely when result_task_ids is an empty list; only call it when result_task_ids is None (DAG-authored default) or a non-empty list
candidates.trigger: await self._serialize_xcoms() called unconditionally or without checking result_task_ids == []

candidates.rule: An Execution API FastAPI route's declared `status_code` must match every HTTP status code the handler actually returns; all non-default success codes must appear in the `responses` dict
candidates.trigger: FastAPI route decorator has `status_code=HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT` (or similar) but the handler also returns a different 2xx status, or a new status code is added to `responses` without updating the route's default `status_code`

candidates.rule: OpenTelemetry span names in the task execution path must embed the executing component (worker or triggerer) as a segment, e.g. `task_run.worker.{task_id}` or `worker.{task_id}`
candidates.trigger: New `tracer.start_span(name=...)` call in task execution routes uses a flat name like `task_run.{task_id}` without a component segment

candidates.rule: Bundle names persisted in `DagBundleModel` rows and emitted in REST API responses must be finalised before the first release that ships them; renaming afterwards requires a DB migration
candidates.trigger: A new auto-generated bundle name string (e.g. via an f-string concatenating package names) is introduced in bundle-discovery code that writes to `DagBundleModel`

candidates.rule: Columns added to SQLAlchemy `load_only()` clauses must be actually accessed by the downstream code that consumes the query result
candidates.trigger: A column is added to a `load_only(...)` call in a query-builder function but no code path that calls that function reads the newly added column attribute

candidates.rule: Use structlog keyword-argument style for all log calls; do not use `%s` positional format strings as log message arguments
candidates.trigger: A `log.info(...)`, `log.warning(...)`, or similar structlog call passes positional `%s` format arguments instead of keyword arguments for metadata fields

candidates.rule: Config entries in `config.yml` must document the meaning of all special sentinel values (e.g. `0` meaning "disabled" or "unlimited") in the `description` field
candidates.trigger: A new config key with a numeric `default` of `0` (or another sentinel) is added to `config.yml` without the `description` explaining what `0` means

candidates.rule: A config `description` in `config.yml` must not reference Airflow features or model fields that do not exist at HEAD in the same PR
candidates.trigger: A new config key's `description` mentions a field name or feature (e.g. `TaskInstanceDTO.language`) that is not present in the codebase in the same PR

candidates.rule: A new single-entry config section must not be created as a top-level section in `config.yml`; place the entry in the `core` section following the precedent of `xcom_backend` and similar singleton settings
candidates.trigger: A new top-level YAML section is added to `config.yml` containing only one config key, when no further keys are planned

candidates.rule: `VersionChange` subclass names must describe the schema migration performed (what field or model changes), not the behaviour of the old code being replaced
candidates.trigger: A class that subclasses `VersionChange` is named after what the previous code did (e.g. `ValidateSomething`) rather than after the data-model delta (e.g. `ChangeFooToBar`)

candidates.rule: Do not add application-level mutex lock tables to guard writes that SQLite already serialises; skip the lock for SQLite backends
candidates.trigger: A new ORM model used as a mutex lock (e.g. `MutexLock`, `LockTable`) is added and `session.add`/`session.delete` are used around a critical section without a SQLite exemption

candidates.rule: Use `if TYPE_CHECKING: assert x is not None` to narrow a variable's type within a branch rather than widening a downstream function's signature to accept `None`
candidates.trigger: A function's parameter type is widened to `T | None` solely because a caller cannot statically prove the value is non-None at the call site, and the value is known to be non-None at runtime

candidates.rule: Prefer `session.scalar()` or `session.scalars().one()` over `session.get()` with a composite primary-key dict when querying ORM models
candidates.trigger: `session.get(ModelClass, {"key1": val1, "key2": val2})` is used to look up a model with a composite primary key

candidates.rule: Setting `_AIRFLOW_PROCESS_CONTEXT` must be centralised in the `action_cli` decorator (when `check_db=True`), not scattered at individual CLI command call sites
candidates.trigger: A CLI command manually sets or reads `os.environ["_AIRFLOW_PROCESS_CONTEXT"]` inside the command body rather than relying on the `action_cli` decorator

candidates.rule: When adding a new keyword argument to a DB-command callable passed to `run_db_migrate_command`, all concrete implementations of that callable (including `BaseDBManager.upgradedb` and `FABDBManager.upgradedb`) must accept the new kwarg
candidates.trigger: A new `kwarg` is forwarded to a `command(...)` call inside `run_db_migrate_command` but the corresponding `upgradedb` methods on `BaseDBManager` or `FABDBManager` are not updated to accept it

candidates.rule: Only lazy-import a module inside a function body to break an import cycle; stdlib modules (`importlib`, `logging`) must always be imported at module top level
